title: Ordinary and perverse middle extension on a smooth curve
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $C_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected separated curve of finite type over $k_0$, and let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion. Here smooth means [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and curve means pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Put $C=C_0\times_{k_0}k$, $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$, $j:U\hookrightarrow C$, and $Z=C\setminus U$. Let $F_0$ be a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves, def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with underlying geometric sheaf $F$ on $U$. Use the middle-perversity support and cosupport classes [def-per-perverse-subcategories] in $D^b_c(C,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$.

The complex $(j_*F)[1]$, using ordinary sheaf direct image [def-wf-middle-extension] and cohomological shift [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], is perverse. Among perverse extensions of $F[1]$ to $C$, it is uniquely characterized by having no nonzero perverse subobject or quotient whose restriction to $U$ is zero. Thus, denoting this perverse intermediate extension by $j_{!*}(F[1])$, there is a canonical isomorphism
$$j_{!*}(F[1])\simeq(j_*F)[1]$$
restricting to the identity on $F[1]$. The isomorphism is natural in $F$ and compatible with the Weil structure of $F_0$.

source.place: Second paragraph, sentence identifying the curve perverse intermediate extension. This is the theorem implicit in that definition remark; no Stacks tag for perverse sheaves is claimed.

proof.text: The geometric curve $C$ is smooth, separated, of finite type and pure dimension one over the algebraically closed (hence perfect) field $k$, and $\ell$ is invertible. By [lem-sc-dense-open-finite-complement], $Z=C\setminus U$ is a finite set of closed points. Put $A=j_*F$ with the ordinary-direct-image convention of [def-wf-middle-extension]. Clause (4) of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart] gives $A[1]\in\mathrm{Perv}(C)$. The theorem's Weil-pair version applies to the given finite-field data. By [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], $j^*A\cong F$, so this is a perverse extension of $F[1]$.

source.place: Second paragraph, curve intermediate-extension assertion; expanded argument following the return and the curve-heart clauses (3)–(5)

proof.text: First let $B$ be any perverse object with $j^*B=0$. Ordinary t-exactness of $j^*$ in [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] gives $j^*\mathcal H^{-1}B=j^*\mathcal H^0B=0$. Clause (3) of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart] says that $\mathcal H^{-1}B$ has no nonzero punctual subsheaf. It is itself punctual, being supported on the finite boundary from Step 1, and hence is zero. That same clause leaves only $\mathcal H^0B$, and the closed-essential-image assertion of the open–closed lemma writes $B\cong i_*E$ in degree zero for a constructible sheaf $E$ on $Z$. Apply this to a boundary perverse subobject $Q$ of $A[1]$: [lem-dl-a1-boundary-hom-vanishing] makes its monomorphism $i_*E\to A[1]$ zero, whence $Q=0$. For a boundary perverse quotient $R$, the other Hom vanishing makes the epimorphism $A[1]\to i_*E$ zero, whence $R=0$. A zero monomorphism or epimorphism in an abelian category has zero source or target, respectively.

source.place: Second paragraph, curve intermediate-extension assertion; expanded argument following the return and the curve-heart clauses (3)–(5)

proof.text: Let $P\in\mathrm{Perv}(C)$ be any extension, with a specified identification $\alpha:j^*P\xrightarrow{\sim}F[1]$, having no nonzero boundary perverse subobject or quotient. Since $j^*$ is ordinary t-exact by [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], $j^*\mathcal H^0P=\mathcal H^0(F[1])=0$. Clause (5) of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart] gives a perverse epimorphism $P\to(\mathcal H^0P)[0]$. Its target is supported on the boundary, so the hypothesis on quotients forces $\mathcal H^0P=0$. The same exact sequence identifies $P$ canonically with $G[1]$, where $G=\mathcal H^{-1}P$. Clause (3) says that $G$ has no nonzero punctual subsheaf. Taking degree $-1$ of $\alpha$ identifies $j^*G$ with $F$.

source.place: Second paragraph, curve intermediate-extension assertion; expanded argument following the return and the curve-heart clauses (3)–(5)

proof.text: Use the sheaf adjunction of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] to form $u:G\to j_*j^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}j_*F=A$ from the identification $j^*G\cong F$ of Step 3. Its restriction is that identification because $j^*j_*\cong\mathrm{id}$. Exactness of $j^*$ on sheaves therefore makes both $\ker u$ and $T=\operatorname{coker}u$ supported on $Z$. Since $Z$ is finite, $\ker u$ is a punctual subsheaf of $G$ and is zero by Step 3. Thus $0\to G\xrightarrow{u}A\to T\to0$ is short exact in the constructible sheaf heart. The sheaf $T$ is punctual and $j^*T=0$.

source.place: Second paragraph, curve intermediate-extension assertion; expanded argument following the return and the curve-heart clauses (3)–(5)

proof.text: Apply clause (4) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] first to the standard t-structure supplied by [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology]: the sheaf sequence of Step 4 gives a distinguished triangle $G\to A\to T\to G[1]$. Rotating gives $T\to G[1]\xrightarrow{u[1]}A[1]\to T[1]$. All three terms are perverse: $G[1]\cong P$, $A[1]$ by Step 1, and $T$ by clause (3) of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart], since its only cohomology is the punctual sheaf in degree zero. Apply the same clause (4), now to the perverse t-structure of that theorem, to obtain $0\to T\to P\xrightarrow{u[1]}A[1]\to0$ in its heart. The hypothesis on boundary subobjects of $P$ forces $T=0$. Consequently $u[1]$ is an isomorphism restricting to $\alpha$. This proves existence of the comparison for every such $P$, rather than assuming uniqueness in a definition of $j_{!*}$.

source.place: Second paragraph, curve intermediate-extension assertion; expanded argument following the return and the curve-heart clauses (3)–(5)

proof.text: The comparison is unique with its specified restriction. Indeed the standard heart is a full subcategory by [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], and shifting both sides identifies maps $G[1]\to A[1]$ with sheaf maps $G\to j_*F$. The same lemma's adjunction identifies these with maps $j^*G\to F$, so restriction determines the map uniquely. Steps 1–2 supply one extension with the required property and Steps 3–5 identify every other one with it by the unique map inducing its given identification on $U$. This proves the characterization and justifies the notation $j_{!*}(F[1])$ in the statement. For a map $v:F\to F'$, the ordinary map $(j_*v)[1]$ restricts to $v[1]$. For arbitrary choices of characterized extensions of $F[1]$ and $F'[1]$, conjugate this map by their comparisons. The same adjunction, now with target $j_*F'$, says it is the unique map with that restriction. Hence comparison commutes with every $v$ and is natural in $F$.

source.place: Second paragraph, curve intermediate-extension assertion; expanded argument following the return and the curve-heart clauses (3)–(5)

proof.text: For Weil compatibility work with Frobenius pairs as defined in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The Weil-pair clauses of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart] supply the basic object and the exact sequence used to kill $\mathcal H^0P$; its geometric clauses give the preceding isomorphism. The truncation identifications and the sheaf unit defining $u$ commute with Frobenius by the final paragraph of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], since $j_0$ is defined over $k_0$. Thus $u[1]$ intertwines the Frobenius isomorphisms. Equivalently, the two composites from Frobenius pullback of $G[1]$ to $A[1]$ restrict to the same map on $U$; the adjunction argument of Step 6 makes them equal. The inverse of an equivariant isomorphism is equivariant by composing that equality with its inverse. No triangulated structure on the category of Weil pairs is used: Step 5's triangles are in the geometric derived category. Naturality from Step 6 restricts to Weil morphisms because the ordinary units and counits commute with Frobenius.

Item: the seven-step proof is correct. Step 1 shows (j_*F)[1] is perverse using heart clause (4) for the ordinary j_*, the finite complement from lem-sc-dense-open-finite-complement (C is a def-sc-curves curve) and j^*j_*=id. Step 2 shows a boundary perverse B has H^{-1}B punctual, hence 0 by clause (3), so B=i_*E by the essential-image clause of the open-closed lemma; the new lemma then kills boundary subobjects and quotients. Step 3 kills H^0P with the clause (5) epimorphism, so P=G[1]. Step 4 shows ker u is a punctual subsheaf of G, hence 0. Step 5 applies triangle-lemma clause (4) once for the standard t-structure and once for the perverse one: the rotated triangle T->G[1]->A[1] gives the perverse short exact sequence 0->T->P->A[1]->0, so T=0. Step 6 gets uniqueness and naturality from Hom(G[1],A[1])=Hom(j^*G,F). Step 7 gets Weil compatibility from the Frobenius paragraph of the open-closed lemma and the Step 6 adjunction. The coefficient category is the same D^b_c(-,Qlbar) of def-weil-pbc-qbar-category in every node; no base change other than the geometric fibre occurs, and the target statement is unchanged. New node lem-dl-a1-boundary-hom-vanishing: true, checked independently. Hom(A[1],i_*E) is a negative Ext between heart objects. For Hom(i_*E,A[1]), the cone of tau^{<=0}Rj_*F -> Rj_*F lies in D^{>=1}, so Ri^!A is in D^{>=2}. Tested on Z empty, F=0, E=0, and the constant sheaf on G_m inside A^1. B1-B4 hold, all three search kinds are recorded, created and blueprint.from/via are correct, it is not a duplicate (checked prop-a1-curve-perverse-simples, lem-sf-ordinary-triangle-counit-cone (derived j_* only), lem-a1-local-boundary-duality) and not a restated clause.
